content.comment_body: Hello, when interlocking two [product_name] modules, you slide the interlocking mechanism between them. Is it possible to make this connection using a cable instead? We are planning to place the CPU module and extension modules on different DIN rails. Do they have to be installed in-line on the same rail? Thank you in advance.

No, this topic has come up several times before in this forum. There are no suitable connection cables available from [company_name]. Due to the module functions and different voltage classes, multiple cable types and lengths would be required. [company_name] recommends using a separate [product_name] for each DIN rail, and connecting the [product_name] controllers through networking instead. Refer to the video from [company_name] for more details. 2-line configuration.
Understood, that explanation helps. We'll use two [product_name] controllers in a master/slave setup as a solution. Thank you for your quick reply.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are interested in more flexible installation options for [product_name] modules, questioning whether modules must be directly attached or can be connected by a cable to allow placement on separate DIN rails. The discussion clarifies that cable-based connections are not supported, and the design from [company_name] requires using additional controllers for modules on different rails, rather than simple extension via cable.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to connect [product_name] modules with a cable, allowing installation on separate DIN rails. They hope for a straightforward way to link CPU and extension modules across different rails for greater configuration flexibility.
